newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower in welcome consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower in welcome consolidation.

text.p: Swiss shares ended sharply lower on Thursday but dealers said the consolidation after a series of record-hitting sessions was welcome rather than disturbing.
Profit-taking, which was intensified by derivative-linked trading, a lower dollar and weaker-than-expected U.S. jobless claims data, put pressure on prices, one dealer said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended down 1.53 percent or 91.7 points at 5,885.4.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was down 1.39 percent or 52.34 points at 3,700.83.
Bourse volume reached 3.33 billion francs, off from Wednesday's 3.69 billion.

Only a small number of shares gained. Insurer Winterthur, the object of speculative interest amid unconfirmed rumours it could face a takeover bid or strengthen its ties with Credit Suisse, rose 18 francs to 1,438.
One dealer said BZ Bank, which has built up a stake in the insurer, was thought to have bought Winterthur shares and sold shares of Zurich Group.
The market was waiting for more details of BZ Bank's holdings, which are scheduled to be released on Friday morning.
Swiss Re and Gas Vision also posted gains. Registered shares of Swiss Re rose 30 francs to 2,205. Gas Vision advanced six francs to 706.
Financials were weaker. Credit Suisse lost 4.25 francs to 203. Swiss Bank Corp dropped five to 422.

Industrials like Clariant and ABB also belonged to the decliners. ABB, whose shares' par value dropped by 50 francs today, dropped 114 francs or five percent to 2,156. Clariant lost 34 francs and ended at 951.
Pharmaceuticals lost ground. Roche certificates came off lows but still ended 250 francs lower at 14,400. Volume leader Novartis dropped 50 francs to 2,403.
